patch.value:
Source: https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1464

## Problem

A **successful** `pm close <id> "<reason>" --validate-close warn` (exit 0, `status: "closed"`) prints a `recovery:` block containing `suggested_retry` and `suggested_retry_args`. Every other `recovery` / `suggested_retry` an agent sees in pm output belongs to a failed command, so agents read this one as a failure too.

Observed on 2026.10.13 (orchestrator session, 2026-10-14): I closed three items with warn-mode validation. Output piped through `tail -2` showed only the two `suggested_retry*` lines, so I re-ran `pm close`. The retry failed with `Item … is already terminal; use pm update …`: one wasted round trip, an error, and briefly the belief that the close had not happened.

## Repro

```bash
d=$(mktemp -d) && cd "$d" && git init -q && pm init >/dev/null
id=$(pm create --type Task --title "Probe" --description d --acceptance-criteria a --json | jq -r .item.id)
pm close "$id" "done" --validate-close warn; echo "exit=$?"
```

Output (abridged):

```
status: "closed"
warnings[1]: "close_validation_missing_fields:pm-6lay:resolution (--resolution),expected_result (--expected-result),actual_result (--actual-result)"
recovery:
  missing[3]: "--resolution","--expected-result","--actual-result"
  suggested_retry: "pm --pm-path …/.agents/pm update pm-6lay --resolution \"<value>\" --expected-result \"<value>\" --actual-result \"<value>\""
exit=0
```

## Suggested change

1. On success, rename the block to a non-failure key, for example `follow_up:` with `suggested_command`, so `recovery`/`retry` keep their meaning (the command failed, here is how to re-run it).
2. Since `pm close` already accepts `--resolution`, `--expected-result` and `--actual-result`, mention them in the warning and in the generated AGENTS.md quickstart (`pm close <id> "<evidence>" --validate-close warn`). Agents can then close with full evidence in one call instead of close + update.

Related, all closed: #953, #757, #519 (failure-path recovery bundles for `pm close`), #1203.
